title: Archive Inventory (DuckDB)
summary: A DuckDB database containing a complete inventory of the 2TB archive, including file paths, sizes, formats, and checksums. This enables rapid querying of the collection structure without needing the raw files locally.
nextSteps: Integrate DuckDB-WASM into the file explorer for client-side SQL queries.
Automate the generation of this database during archive audits.
Add file-level metadata tags to the database tables.
limitations: The inventory is a snapshot and may not reflect very recent additions to the physical storage.

title: Herefordshire Tithe Maps
summary: Georectified and photographed tithe maps with apportionment material. This is one of the clearest routes into field-name, ownership, land-use, and boundary digitisation work.
nextSteps: Create parish-level inventory with image counts, map status, and apportionment availability.
Publish first curated PMTiles release assets for selected georeferenced maps.
Digitise field boundaries and link polygons to apportionment rows.
Document georectification confidence and known distortions.
limitations: Many originals are photographed or scanned as raw/TIF/JPG files and need normalisation before web delivery.

title: Historic Aerial Photography
summary: Historic aerial photography including Aerofilms, NMRC/AP material, Environment Agency/English Nature imagery, and local photographic sets.
nextSteps: Generate a photograph inventory with dates, sources, approximate footprints, and rights notes.
Create web thumbnails and lower-resolution JPEG/WebP access copies.
Identify image sets suitable for georeferencing or oblique-photo annotation.
Separate raw archival images from public preview derivatives.
limitations: The collection includes large TIFFs and camera raw files that are not appropriate for git or direct static hosting.

title: Habitat and Hedgerow Surveys
summary: Long-term ecological and habitat material, including hedgerows, grassland, orchards, LWS criteria, plant records, and habitat mapping.
nextSteps: Identify canonical spreadsheets/databases and separate them from duplicated exports.
Convert priority vector layers to GeoPackage and simplified GeoJSON.
Document sensitive ecological records before public release.
Create a timeline of survey methods and organisational context.
limitations: The raw folder structure mixes reports, photos, GIS files, and working material.

title: Public Records and Exchequer Material
summary: Scans, references, and working material relating to Exchequer records, legal documents, estate material, and early modern public records.
nextSteps: Inventory record references and image sequences.
Prioritise transcription and translation tasks.
Link references to parishes, estates, fields, and people where possible.
Define citation and rights guidance for public use.
limitations: Records need scholarly interpretation before they become useful datasets.

title: Woodland and 1948 Landscape Survey Material
summary: Woodland cover and post-war landscape material, including FC1953ecw, Ancient Woodland data, DEM/LIDAR context, and related map layers.
nextSteps: Clarify which source files correspond to 1948 survey evidence versus later derived mapping.
Convert suitable raster layers to PMTiles or COGs.
Publish a woodland-change research brief.
Cross-reference with aerial photography and tithe-era woodland boundaries.
limitations: The 1948 evidence appears distributed across several map and derived-data folders.

title: Royal Commission and Parish Survey Material
summary: Parish-level survey material and related historical archive scans from the Royal Commission era and adjacent collections.
nextSteps: Split the broad History folder into coherent public collection records.
Create parish-level index pages.
Identify high-value documents for transcription and geocoding.
Connect survey records to map and aerial-photo evidence.
limitations: The broad History folder needs deeper curation before public browsing is practical.

title: River Wye and NRA Archive
summary: Historic maps, bridge and flood photographs, NRA records, and Wye corridor material for river-management and landscape-change research.
nextSteps: Create a River Wye sub-catalog by place and record type.
Georeference bridge, flood, and river-plan material.
Build a research timeline linking flood events, infrastructure, and land management.
Prepare public download bundles for cleaned metadata.
limitations: The material spans several archive folders and needs normalised place names.
